Subject: Demo request — GitHub Actions / OSS integration

Hi Diego,

I signed up for a trial today (Foobar Labs) and flagged interest in integrations with GitHub Actions and some OSS tooling. We're looking at automating model inference as part of our CI pipeline — basically triggering small inference runs for inference tests and embedding generation for PR descriptions.

Quick context: we're a YC-backed infra startup, small infra team (2 engs), evaluating both hosted APIs and private deployment. Important points for us: GitHub App vs OAuth for auth, rate limits for bursts from Actions, and whether Redwood can run in our cloud account or if we have to use the hosted API initially.

Would love a short demo next week to see how Redwood would slot into our CI flow. Availability: Tue/Wed afternoons PST are best for me.

Thanks,
Sam

Diego — thanks for the quick reply.

Those times look good; the Tue 3:30pm slot is ideal if you can do it. A couple of pre-demo questions so we can surface them during the call:

1) Auth: we'd prefer a GitHub App (for org-level installs) but want to understand token exchange. Can Redwood accept a GitHub App JWT and exchange it server-side to scoped tokens?
2) Rate limiting: our CI runs can spike when many PRs open. How do you handle bursty requests from Actions (are there client-side backoff recommendations, or server ingress controls)?
3) Deployment: for POC, we'd probably use hosted API, but long term would consider Private in our GCP account. Is there an onboarding path that lets us start hosted then move to Private without changing client code?

Also, can you loop in someone from pre-sales/solutions engineering for the technical details? If so, we can cover the above items without digging into low-level knobs.

Appreciate it — see you Tue 2026-12-01 3:30pm PST if that works for you.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the intro, Diego — happy to run this. Confirming Tue 2026-12-01 3:30–4:00pm PST. I created a calendar invite (Google Meet) and attached a short quickstart PDF that shows the typical Actions workflow. Link below.

Proposed 30-minute agenda:
- 0–5m: Intro + goals from Foobar Labs
- 5–15m: Live demo — GitHub Actions -> Redwood hosted API flow (showing token exchange example)
- 15–25m: Discuss auth options (GitHub App, OAuth, service accounts) and migration path to Private (high-level steps)
- 25–30m: Q&A + next steps (POC plan & follow-ups)

Short answers to Sam's pre-asks (we'll cover in detail in the demo):
1) Auth: We support GitHub App install flow. For private installs we recommend using the GitHub App to mint short-lived tokens and then do a server-side exchange to a Redwood API key via our token-exchange endpoint (demo snippet included in the PDF).
2) Rate limiting: Redwood's hosted ingress has burst capacity and autoscaling; for GitHub Actions we recommend client-side exponential backoff with jitter for retries and batching PR embedding jobs where possible. We can show examples of batching in the demo.
3) Deployment migration: yes — the client SDKs are the same. You can start with hosted (API key) and flip a config flag to point to a Private endpoint or Dedicated hostname; we keep the same client call patterns, so minimal code change.

Attachments: redwood-inference-quickstart.pdf (10 pages)
